about: Every fork edit to a file that also exists upstream needs a row here.
One physical path per row. Globs are rejected by the checker.
status 'planned' means the row is forward-declared from the implementation
plan and the path has not been touched yet; flip it to 'modified' in the same
commit that first changes the file, and say what invariant the edit implements.
Genuinely new fork-owned paths are not listed row by row; they must fall under
a declared prefix in fork_owned_areas, which the checker reports separately.

owners.channel: Channel identity, feature policy, paths and exhaustive match sites.
owners.services-boundary: Compile boundary between local product and upstream hosted services.
owners.identity: Branding, marks, URI scheme, menus and installer identity.
owners.materials: Renderer chrome policy, bevels, theme and material coverage.
owners.plate: Status plate geometry, data adapter and workspace integration.
owners.packaging: Platform bundle scripts and artifact manifests.
owners.ci: Fork CI workflows and verification scripts.

Fork binary wrapper that sets the channel before entering the app.
Fork channel assets, icons, desktop metadata and version source.
Fork product policy, startup, branding, theme, chrome and plate integration.
Fork GUI integration cases built with the Doom Term policy.
Pure plate geometry, glyph data, presentation state and pixel operations.
Read-only local session discovery, association, capture and activity.
Public-only CI environment setup with no upstream credentials.
Fork CI and release workflows, kept separate from the upstream ones.

rows.reason: Turn the `doomterm` + `warp_services` combination into a compile error. The two are different products built from one tree, and allowing both would leave 'is this build local-only?' as a runtime question that a shipped binary cannot be audited against.

rows.reason: Select DOOMTERM_FEATURES, a closed allowlist, instead of the union of Cargo-selected flags, channel additions and RELEASE_FLAGS. Under a union a flag added upstream arrives enabled and someone must notice; under an allowlist it arrives disabled and someone must choose it. The list starts empty so each entry is a claim that the capability was tested.
rows.validation: crates/warp_core/src/channel/state_tests.rs subprocess test; the allowlist is asserted empty until entries are added with their own acceptance tests.

rows.reason: Group server and Oz configuration into an optional HostedServicesConfig so that 'this build has no hosted services' is expressible. Previously both were required, so a local-only channel had to name production URLs it would never contact, which from the outside is indistinguishable from a build that has simply not made a request yet. Flattened on the wire so existing channel configuration files parse unchanged.
rows.validation: crates/warp_core/src/channel/config_tests.rs: historical-shape parse, absent-fields parse, both round trips, and the assertion that an absent configuration emits no server_config or oz_config keys at all.

rows.reason: Read hosted configuration through the new option; make init() channel-aware so the pre-`set` default is not upstream's production endpoints in a Doom Term build; return an option from server_root_domain, which previously unwrapped a parse with `expect` that would now be a startup panic; and add url_scheme_for as a pure seam so per-channel policy can be tested without mutating the process-global singleton.
rows.validation: channel::state_tests, including a subprocess test that asserts the real global state of a Doom Term binary and that a server URL override cannot create a configuration.

rows.reason: Remove a startup panic. `create_oauth_client` parsed the server root URL with an `expect`, which was sound only while every channel had one baked in. With no hosted services the parse fails and the panic fired inside ServerApi::new, crashing the application before any window appeared. Observed in a real Doom Term launch, not predicted. Absence now yields None and the device flow reports an explicit error where someone actually tries to sign in.
rows.validation: Verified by launching the Doom Term binary: it previously exited 101 at this line and now reaches a rendered window. cargo test -p warp_server_client covers the OAuth client test.

rows.reason: Follow the OAuth client becoming optional. The test asserts the client is present under a channel that has hosted services, so a None there would mean the test build lost its server configuration rather than that the client ID changed.
